A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViDiT-Q and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Shared experiments and relocated material can be matched reliably despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video quantization experiments, component ablations, and memory/latency profiling in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original quantization evaluations and adds super-resolution, lower-bitwidth, hardware and mixed-precision experiments in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: v1 uses timestep-aware channel scaling with separate alpha values for two denoising halves (Section 3.2.3). v3 replaces this with static-dynamic balancing: scaling addresses initial channel imbalance, followed by orthogonal/Hadamard rotation to handle time-varying imbalance (Section 4.2). This changes a central quantization component.

E1.justification: v3 adds a distinct image super-resolution task using InfDiT on DIV2K validation data (Appendix D.2), extending beyond v1's image/video generation coverage. COCO, VBench, OpenSORA prompts and UCF-101 remain represented; UCF-101 and Latte results move to Appendix D.1.

E2.justification: v3 adds Q-DiT, PTQ4DiT and QuaRot to OpenSORA comparisons and substantially expands the VBench and COCO comparator sets. UCF-101/STDiT gains Q-Diffusion and SmoothQuant rows, and Appendix D.5 adds AdaRound/BRECQ. PTQ4DM and ZeroQuant disappear from the OpenSORA numerical comparison, although they remain discussed.

E3.justification: Hardware evaluation changes from v1's reported RTX 4080/static-INT8 proxy profiling to implemented kernels on A100, with additional RTX 3090 and Orin measurements. v3 introduces W4A4/W2A8 mixed configurations and a bicubic 4x DIV2K evaluation protocol. Main OpenSORA comparisons also switch from raw Flow Score to reported Delta Flow Score.

E4.justification: v1's staged dynamic/scaling/timestep-aware ablation is replaced and expanded with scaling-only, rotation-only, static-dynamic and mixed-precision alternatives (v3 Table 2 and Figure 8). Appendix E.3/Table 8 adds comparisons of MSE, joint-metric and decoupled search. Lower-bitwidth and SageAttention compatibility tests provide further supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. Both primarily present point estimates; the revised sensitivity-score normalization does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial baseline, super-resolution, lower-bitwidth and search-ablation results. Table 4, for example, reports W4A8 InfDiT PSNR/SSIM of 26.0139/0.7249. Hardware reporting changes from v1's 1.47x estimated speedup to 1.71x W8A8 and 1.38x W4A8 measurements under different hardware/implementations. Many shared VBench, UCF-101 and PixArt-alpha scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Compared with v1's brief quantization/scaling formulas, v3 adds a formal layerwise surrogate objective, a mu-coherence definition and rounding/clipping-error reasoning in Section 3.1. Rotation-invariance and quantized-GEMM identities also appear. These are limited formal additions rather than a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central accuracy/compression goal remains, but v3's abstract and contribution list add implemented GPU kernels and practical end-to-end acceleration as explicit contributions. The introduction also recasts the methodological contribution around quantization-error analysis and static-dynamic balancing, replacing v1's emphasis on timestep-aware scaling.

C2.justification: v3 explains time-varying imbalance through feature modulation, separating the learned scale-shift table from timestep embeddings; v1 mainly observes the variation. It adds explanations of baseline and mixed-precision-search failures, and discusses compute-bound W4A8 execution, weight upcasting and lower-bit hardware constraints (Sections 4.2, 5.3 and Appendices D.4/E.3).

D1.justification: v3 adds baseline implementation details, quantization/Hadamard kernel-fusion information, profiling-step disclosure, DIV2K cropping/patch settings and low-bit layer proportions. Its reproducibility statement says code and videos accompany supplementary materials, replacing v1's video-webpage pointer; availability is not independently established by the PDFs. v1's calibration and sensitivity-analysis runtime estimates are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: v1 states that no prior research investigated DiT quantization. v3 explicitly positions itself against Q-DiT and PTQ4DiT, distinguishing text-conditioned generation from their earlier settings. It adds substantive discussion of rotation-based quantization, incoherence processing, attention acceleration, caching and sampling methods, substantially revising the research context.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten. v3 separates Preliminary Analysis from the proposed method, reorganizes experimental discussion, moves UCF-101 material into the appendix and introduces dedicated additional-results and analysis appendices. These changes substantially alter the document's explanatory structure.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the framework, channel-balancing and mixed-precision diagrams, expands comparison-table structures and replaces the hardware plots. It relocates the UCF-101 table and adds super-resolution, lower-bitwidth, device-comparison and GEMM illustrations. Several VBench example figures are retained, while image-generation examples and their comparison layout are replaced.

improvement.justification: Implemented W8A8/W4A8 kernels replace v1's proxy timing evidence, while specialized DiT baselines and stronger component/search ablations substantially improve deployment and methodological validation. Super-resolution testing strengthens applicability. These gains outweigh reporting problems, including inconsistent FlowScore labeling and Table 5's ambiguous PixArt-Sigma attribution despite repeating PixArt-alpha values. The timing changes do not establish a same-setting speedup over v1.
